lockScreen.errMismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
lockScreen.unlockIntro: Your seed is encrypted on this device. Enter your passphrase to unlock it.
lockScreen.plaintextIntro: This wallet's seed is currently stored unencrypted on this computer — anyone with access to the file could spend your funds. Set a passphrase now and it will be encrypted in place. Your balance and history are not affected.
lockScreen.chooseIntro: Choose a passphrase. It encrypts your wallet's seed on this computer, so the files left on disk are useless to anyone who copies them.
lockScreen.noReset: There is no way to reset this passphrase — it is never sent anywhere and never stored. If you forget it, the only way back into this wallet is your seed phrase or a backup file, so keep one of those safe.
lockScreen.haveBackup: Already have a backup file? Restore from backup

restoreFromBackup.errDeviceMin: The device passphrase needs at least 8 characters.
restoreFromBackup.errDeviceMismatch: The two device passphrases do not match.
restoreFromBackup.title: Restore from backup
restoreFromBackup.intro: Open an encrypted backup file and set it up on this computer.
restoreFromBackup.filePassPlaceholder: The passphrase you gave the file
restoreFromBackup.rebuildNote: Your balance rebuilds from the chain after restoring — this takes a minute or two.

appLockScreen.wrongSecret: That {{secret}} does not unlock this wallet.
appLockScreen.offerBody: Use your fingerprint to open ZKas instead of typing your {{secret}}. Your {{secret}} still works and is what secures your keys — the fingerprint just unlocks the app on this device, and it never leaves the phone.
appLockScreen.title: Unlock ZKas
appLockScreen.intro: Your wallet key is encrypted on this device. Enter your {{secret}} to use it.
appLockScreen.forgotten: Forgotten it? There is nothing to reset — the {{secret}} is never stored or sent anywhere. The only way back is restoring each wallet from its seed or a backup file.
appLockScreen.wipeWarning: This erases every wallet's data from this device — the coins stay on-chain, but each wallet comes back only from its seed or backup file.

firstRunNode.errEnterAddress: Enter the address of your node (host:port).
firstRunNode.title: Choose how to connect
firstRunNode.intro: Your keys stay on this computer whichever you pick, and your payments stay shielded on the chain. What differs is who can see your activity, and how soon your balance shows.
firstRunNode.optRemote: This computer · public node — runs the wallet here; nothing about your wallet leaves this computer. First sync scans the chain and takes a while.
firstRunNode.optHosted: Public service — ready at once. The wallet service can see your transactions, not your keys.
firstRunNode.optTor: Over Tor — the public service, with your IP hidden. It still sees your transactions. Needs Tor running on this computer.
firstRunNode.optCustom: My own node — a node you already run, anywhere on your network.
firstRunNode.managedLater: You can install and switch to a fully managed local node from the Node page later.
firstRunNode.stillConnecting: Still connecting — it may be slow or busy right now.
firstRunNode.opensNow: Your wallet opens now on the engine on this computer. You can change how it connects under Settings.
firstRunNode.changeLater: You can change this at any time under Settings, without touching your wallet or its balance.

firstRunConnect.errEngine: The on-device engine could not start on this phone.
firstRunConnect.errEnterAddress: Enter the address of your wallet service (host:port, or an .onion).
firstRunConnect.title: Set up your wallet
firstRunConnect.intro: Nothing leaves this device until you tap. Pick where your wallet connects.
firstRunConnect.publicDesc: Fast, nothing to install. The wallet daemon can see your transactions.
firstRunConnect.torDesc: Hides your IP. The daemon still sees your transactions. Needs Orbot.
firstRunConnect.customDesc: A wallet daemon you run yourself.
firstRunConnect.changeLater: You can change any of this later in Settings, without touching your wallet or its balance.

orbotHelp.nativeIntro: The wallet reaches the onion through Orbot, the free Tor app. It isn't running:
orbotHelp.stepInstallIos: Install Orbot from the App Store.
orbotHelp.stepConnectIos: Open it and connect — Orbot runs as a VPN on iPhone, so allow the VPN configuration it asks for.
orbotHelp.stepVpnMode: Open it and turn on VPN mode.
orbotHelp.stepRetry: Come back and tap Connect over Tor again.
orbotHelp.desktopTitle: Tor isn't running on this computer
orbotHelp.desktopIntro: The wallet connects through Tor's own SOCKS port, so nothing has to be routed system-wide — Tor just has to be running. Start the Tor service, or simply open Tor Browser and leave it open, then try again.
orbotHelp.desktopPorts: It looks on 127.0.0.1:9050 (Tor service) and 127.0.0.1:9150 (Tor Browser).
orbotHelp.desktopOwnNode: For privacy without Tor, run your own node from the Node page — then nobody else sees what you ask.
orbotHelp.browserTitle: Open this wallet in Tor Browser
orbotHelp.browserIntro: An ordinary browser cannot reach an .onion address. The whole wallet is served over Tor — open it in Tor Browser at:
orbotHelp.browserKeys: Your keys stay on your device either way.

runOnPhoneOption.title: Run on this phone
runOnPhoneOption.desc: Most private. No daemon ever sees your transactions. A bit more battery.
runOnPhoneOption.nodeHint: Node to sync from — host:port. The default is the public ZKas node.
runOnPhoneOption.torDesc: Hides your IP from the node. Requires the Orbot app (Tor) running on this phone.

whatsNew.title: Recovery phrases
whatsNew.phraseDesc: New wallets use a standard BIP-39 phrase instead of a 64-character seed. Your existing seed keeps working.
whatsNew.accountsDesc: Add accounts from one phrase — one backup covers them all.
whatsNew.torDesc: Connect over an onion so the service never sees your IP.

errorBoundary.title: Something went wrong
errorBoundary.body: The wallet display hit an error. Your wallet and funds are not affected — reloading almost always fixes this.

bootGuard.couldNotStart: The wallet could not start. It needs site storage (cookies / site data) enabled for this site — your wallet and its settings live there. Allow it for {{host}}, then reload.
